Connectivity: what OPC UA, MQTT and Azure IoT Operations solve

The tag naming trap and why ERP and MES do different jobs

Context: asset, process, order, material and quality
Standards, ontologies, knowledge graphs and semantic governance
Data quality, Fabric, contextualization, Azure Digital Twins and time

takeaways: Connectivity with OPC UA, MQTT and a unified namespace moves signals reliably, but integration requires linking each event to assets, operations, work orders, material, quality and demand.
Names and topic paths are aliases, not identities: governed identifiers, ontologies, data contracts and clear ownership keep meaning intact across ERP, MES, maintenance and quality.
Azure IoT Operations, Microsoft Fabric and Azure Digital Twins provide the edge, data and relationship layers, but relationships must be time-aware and modeled deliberately around a real decision.
hook: A packaging machine stops, every system is connected, and still nobody can say which customer shipment is at risk. This episode is for manufacturing IT/OT architects and data teams who have invested in connectivity but still answer key questions with phone calls and spreadsheets. Learn how to move from moving signals to connecting meaning with context models, knowledge graphs and the Azure industrial stack.
